locations.text: The preregistered primary endpoint asks whether \emph{joint observation} improves token recovery over a forward-only attacker by a practical margin of two percentage points. Both use candidate set $k{=}32$ at depth $L{=}6$ under the public head and an identical budget. Joint observation combines forward activations with true backward gradients, following the bidirectional mechanism established for split-LLM fine-tuning by BiSR \cite{bisr2024}. The contrast averages attack seeds first and then bootstraps crossed document $\times$ victim-run units (10 victim runs $\times$ 256 documents, 100{,}000 replicates, prespecified seed); the 256 evaluation documents are a fixed held-out set reused across arms, so the interval quantifies document and victim-training variability rather than the sampling of fresh text.

The forward--backward reconstruction mechanism is established in BiSR \cite{bisr2024}; our v3 result measures that mechanism with an independent attack design. Published-setting BiSR reproduction remains unestablished because the original processed SensiReplaced inputs are unavailable. The \href{https://github.com/geopolitis/llm-attacker/blob/submission-candidate-20260922-r2/paper/paper_b/main.pdf}{companion framework study} reports matched single-seam implementation conformance and a separately frozen comparison against that adaptation using distinct budgets. Those results do not establish the original dual-cut setting or equal-budget superiority over published BiSR. Other work examines split-inference leakage \cite{fan2026serversee}, dual-sided prompt and response recovery \cite{gu2026pidi}, and structured forward-pass protection \cite{dpforward2023}. We do not evaluate those systems directly. Our input-side observations do not measure generated-response leakage or the broader deployment surfaces covered by Paper~B.

locations.text: The model is GPT-2, using the same pinned 32-token input partitions as v3: 32 calibration documents, 128 training documents and 256 held-out evaluation documents. Each run takes 128 AdamW \cite{loshchilov2019adamw} steps, batch size one, learning rate $5\times10^{-5}$, on one seed-shuffled pass over the training partition. The trainable range is $[b,b+s)$; the observed seam is after $\max(1,b)$ blocks. Thus starts zero and one share a seam, while larger starts change both the trainable range and the observed boundary. The start effect is not an isolated intervention on training location with observation depth held fixed. $D_0$ quantises both forward and backward wires to eight bits; $D_1$ uses four-bit quantisation, gradient clipping at 1.0 and gradient noise of scale 0.1. Utility is held-out cross-entropy relative to the paired all-local final model, $\Delta_U=\mathcal L_{\rm segment}-\mathcal L_{\rm all\ local}$. The frozen pretrained loss is also retained. Final-state evaluation captures forward and backward wires without optimiser updates and retains changed victim parameters for replay.
